Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:14:1.hebrew: קנין דברים הוא - ואין חליפין קונין אלא דבר הנקנה: או מכר, או מתנה, או שעבוד קרקעות שהקנין חל עליו, או מטלטלין:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:14:1.english: It is [merely] an acquisition of words - And [the act of] exchange (chalifin) effects acquisition only of a thing that is acquirable: either a sale, or a gift, or the obligation of real estate, upon which the acquisition takes effect, or movable property.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:14:2.hebrew: ברוחות - זה בורר לו חלק מזרחי, וזה בורר לו חלק מערבי, וקנו מידם. ומעתה, נקנה חלק מזרחי לזה, ואין לזה חלק בו, וכן השני לחבירו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:14:2.english: By directions - This one chooses for himself an eastern portion, and that one chooses for himself a western portion, and they performed a kinyan by their hands. From then on, the eastern portion is acquired by this one, and the other has no share in it, and likewise the second with respect to his fellow.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:14:3.hebrew: והחזיק - בחלקו רפק ביה פורתא, וקרקע נקנה בחזקה אחרי אשר רצו בשעת חלוקה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:14:3.english: And he took possession - In his portion, he leaned on it a little; and land is acquired through taking possession, after they had agreed at the time of the division.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:15:1.hebrew: אריח - חצי לבינה. והלבינה, ג' טפחים; והאריח, טפח ומחצה. ועובי הכותל — אריח מכאן ואריח מכאן, וטפח באמצע שנותן שם טיט לחברו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:15:1.english: Arich - Half a brick. A brick is three handbreadths, and an arich is a handbreadth and a half. The thickness of the wall is an arich from here and an arich from there, and one handbreadth in the middle, where one places mortar to join them.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:15:2.hebrew: לבינים ליבני - שלימות, לבינה לעובי הכותל:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:15:2.english: Bricks – let them build [with bricks] - Whole [bricks], one brick for the thickness of the wall.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:16:1.hebrew: למורשא דקרנת' - ראשי האבנים בולטות לחוץ, שאינן חלקות, ולהכי בעי רוחב טפח יתירא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:16:1.english: For the projection of the corner - The tops of the stones protrude outward, as they are not smooth, and therefore it requires an additional handbreadth of width.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:16:2.hebrew: לביני אורבי - בין דימוס שמכאן ובין דימוס שמכאן, ונותן טיט באמצע:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:16:2.english: For the spaces between the rows - Between the row [of stones] from here and the row from here, and he puts mortar in the middle.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:19:1.english: So we read: Say [that it refers] to bricks that are not planed.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:1:1.hebrew: דאיצטנע מינך - דברי הצנע. אבל חצר החלוקה, לתרוייהו קביעא תשמישתי' לכל אחד בחלקו כל שעה, ולא עבדי בה מילי דצנעא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:1:1.english: That was concealed from you - Private matters. But a divided courtyard — its use is fixed for both of them, each one in his own portion at all times, and they do not do private things in it.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:21:1.english: "We learn from this" etc. - And there is a practical difference for one who accepted upon himself to build a wall for his fellow.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:21:2.english: Birichsa - Small stones and mortar between the two courses (dimosot).

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:22:1.hebrew: למימרא דבגזית כו' כל ד' אמות גובה אי הוה פותיא ה' טפחים קאי ואי לא לא קאי - כדתנן במתני': בגזית זה נותן טפחיים ומחצה וזה נותן טפחיים ומחצה. וקתני סיפא: מחייבין אותן לבנותו עד ד' אמות. ולפי חשבון זה, לגובה שמנה — צריך י' טפחים רוחב:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:22:1.english: Is this to say that it is with hewn stone, etc. — for every four cubits of height, if the width is five handbreadths it stands, and if not it does not stand - As we learned in the mishnah: with hewn stone, this one contributes two and a half handbreadths and that one contributes two and a half handbreadths. And the latter clause teaches: we compel them to build it up to four cubits. And according to this calculation, for a height of eight [cubits], ten handbreadths of width are needed.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:22:2.hebrew: והא אמה טרקסין - דבנין שלמה דגזית הוה, דכתיב אבני גזית (מלכים א ה׳:ל״א), והוי שלשים אמה קומתה, ואין עוביו אלא אמה, להבדיל בין ההיכל לקדשי הקדשים:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:22:2.english: But the cubit of the traksin - The building of Solomon was of hewn stone (gazit), as it is written, "hewn stones" (I Kings 5:31), and its height was thirty cubits, yet its thickness was only one cubit, to separate between the Sanctuary [Heikhal] and the Holy of Holies.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:22:3.hebrew: דאיכא טפח יתירא - ומשום האי טפי פותיא מצי לאגבוה טובא, ואין צריך לתת לכל ארבע אמות ה' טפחים רוחב:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:22:3.english: For there is an extra handbreadth - And because of this additional width, one can raise [the wall] much higher, and one need not give five handbreadths of width for every four cubits [of height].

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:24:1.hebrew: בבנין - שהיה גובהו מאה אמות, כדתנן במסכת מדות (פרק ד מ"ו):
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:24:1.english: In the building - For its height was one hundred cubits, as we learned in tractate Middot (chapter 4, mishna 6).

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:2:1.hebrew: כיון דרצו - לחלוק. ולקמן פריך: מאי איריא רצו? אפילו לא רצו, הרי הן יכולין לכוף זה את זה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:2:1.english: Since they wanted - to divide. And below [the Gemara] challenges: Why specifically [say] "they wanted"? Even if they did not want to, they can compel one another.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:2:2.english: They build a wall - of stones.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:3:1.hebrew: גודא - כותל אבנים. ובחצר שיש בה דין חלוקה, ועל כרחן חולקים:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:3:1.english: A gudda - A wall of stones. [The mishnah speaks] of a courtyard that has the law of division, and they divide it against their will.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:4:1.hebrew: וטעמא דרצו - שהתנו לחולקה בכותל אבנים. הא לא רצו, אין מחייבין אותו אלא מסיפס בעלמא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:4:1.english: And the reason is that they agreed - That they stipulated to divide it with a stone wall. But if they did not agree, we do not obligate him [to build] anything other than a mere [light] partition of plaster-work.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:5:1.english: As people say, etc. - This is the answer.

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:6:1.hebrew: שאין בה דין חלוקה - ח' אמות לא יחלוקו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:6:1.english: That has no law of division - [A courtyard of] eight cubits, they shall not divide [it].

Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:8:1.hebrew: ובכתבי הקדש - ספר תורה שהוא בכרך אחד. וכן נביאים וכתובים הכתובים בגליון כס"ת:
Rashi on Bava Batra 3a:8:1.english: And in the Holy Writings - A Torah scroll that is in a single volume. And likewise Prophets and Writings that are written on a parchment sheet like a Torah scroll.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:13:1.hebrew: כי רצו מאי הוי ניהדרו בהו - למ"ד מחיצה גודא לא פריך, דאיכא למימר דקנו ושיעבדו נכסיהן לבנין הכותל. אלא למ"ד פלוגתא — לא מהני קנין, דקנין דברים בעלמא הוא, דלא מסיק אדעתיה שקנו ברוחות:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:13:1.english: "Even if they wanted [to divide it], what of it? Let them retract from it" - According to the one who says that "partition" means a wall (*guda*), [the Gemara] does not ask [this question], for one can say that they made a *kinyan* and obligated their property for the building of the wall. But according to the one who says that it refers to a division [of the courtyard], a *kinyan* does not help, for it is a mere *kinyan* of words, since [the party] did not seriously intend it, as if they had made the acquisition [with nothing but] winds.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:14:1.hebrew: קנין דברים בעלמא הוא - בפרק השוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף צד.): דתנן, מתנה ש"ח להיות כשואל, ומוקי לה בקנו מידו. התם לאו קנין דברים הוא, אלא קנין גמור הוא, שמשעבד את עצמו שאם יאנס שישלם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:14:1.english: It is merely a verbal acquisition - In the chapter "HaSokher et HaPoalim" (Bava Metzia 94a): For we learned, "If an unpaid bailee stipulated to be [liable] like a borrower," and [the Gemara] establishes it as a case where they performed a *kinyan* by handshake. There it is not a mere verbal acquisition, but rather a full acquisition, for he obligates himself, [such] that if the item is lost to circumstances beyond his control, he will pay:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:14:2.hebrew: רב אשי אמר כגון שהלך כו' - תימה לר"י: מה בא רב אשי להוסיף? וכי איצטריך לאשמועינן דחזקה מועלת כמו קנין? ונראה לר"י דהא קמ"ל: דאע"ג דקאמר לקמן בחזקת הבתים (בבא בתרא דף נג.) שלא בפניו צריך למימר לו "לך חזק וקני", הכא, כיון שאמרו "אתה תקח רוח צפונית ואני רוח דרומית", והלך והחזיק לו כל אחד בשלו, זה שלא בפני זה — נעשה כמי שקנו מידם ברוחות, אע"פ שלא אמרו זה לזה "לך חזק וקני":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:14:2.english: Rav Ashi said: for example, where he went, etc. - R. Yitzchak (the Ri) found this puzzling: What is Rav Ashi coming to add? Was it necessary to teach us that taking possession (chazakah) is effective just like a kinyan? And it appears to the Ri that this is what [Rav Ashi] teaches us: Even though [the Gemara] says later, in the chapter on *Chezkat HaBatim* (Bava Batra 53a), that when [the buyer is] not in the seller's presence, [the seller] must say to him, "Go, take possession and acquire," here, since they said, "You take the northern side and I the southern side," and each one went and took possession of his own [portion], one not in the presence of the other — it is considered as though they had made a kinyan by handshake over [the division of] the sides, even though they did not say to one another, "Go, take possession and acquire."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:22:1.hebrew: ארבע אמות גובה אפותיא דה' קאי טפי לא קאי - וקשיא לר"ת: הא לבינין דגריעי קאי בשלשה טפחים, ועוד: הא קא חזינן דקאי בגזית טפי אפורתא. ותירץ דהכי קאמר: טפי לא קאי כמשפט גזית, שרוצים בני אדם לבנותו שיעמוד ימים רבים כשבונים בגזית:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:22:1.english: Four cubits in height, on a thickness of five [handbreadths] it stands; [any] more, it does not stand - And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: Behold, bricks, which are inferior, stand on three handbreadths [of thickness]. Moreover, we see that [a wall] of hewn stone stands [at a height of] somewhat more [than four cubits]. And he answered that this is what [the Gemara] means: [any] more, it does not stand, according to the standard of hewn stone [construction], for people want it to stand for many years when they build with hewn stone.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:22:2.hebrew: טרקסין - אומר ר"ת דטרק הוי כמו טרוקי גלי, ברכות (דף כח.), וסין הוי סיני; כלומר, שהיה מפסיק וסוגר את הלוחות שנתנו בסיני, שהיו מונחות בארון שהיה בבית קדשי הקדשים. וי"מ: טרקסין — פנים וחוץ, שאותה אמה היתה ספק אם מקודשת פנים או חוץ, ולכך היו שם שתי פרוכת, כדאמרינן ביומא (דף נא:):
Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:22:2.english: Traksin - Rabbeinu Tam says that trak is like troki in "troki gali" (Berakhot 28a) [i.e., "lock" or "shut"], and sin is [short for] Sinai. That is to say, it separated and closed off the tablets that were given at Sinai, which were placed in the ark that was in the Holy of Holies. And some explain: traksin means "inside and outside," for that cubit [of space] was uncertain whether it was sanctified as inside [the Holy of Holies] or as outside, and therefore there were two curtains there, as we say in Yoma (51b):

Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:22:3.english: It is different there, since there is an extra handbreadth - [The Gemara] could have answered [differently], that [the wall] stands more securely on account of the ceiling and the plaster, as we say shortly below:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:7:1.hebrew: מאי קא משמע לן בשאין בה דין חלוקה - אע"ג דקא משמע לן דשמיה היזק, ה"פ: מאי קמ"ל במאי דאיירי באין בה דין חלוקה? לישמעינן בשיש בה דין חלוקה, [אע"ג דלא רצו] (כשרצו) פלגי! תימה, הא קמ"ל דאפילו באין בה דין חלוקה, דאיכא למימר "על מנת לעשות גודא לא איתרצאי", כדפירש לעיל:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 3a:7:1.english: "What does this teach us, [in a case] where it has no law of division?" - Even though [the Mishnah] teaches us that [visual intrusion] is called "damage," this is the meaning [of the question]: What does it teach us by discussing a case where it has no law of division? Let it teach us [the law] in a case where it does have the law of division, [even though they did not agree] (when they agreed), they divide! One might be puzzled [by this question]; but it teaches us this: that even in a case where there is no law of division, since one can say, "I did not agree on the condition of building a wall," as [Rashi] explained above.
